description: The plot titled “Search Space of M-Cube” illustrates the growth in the number of possible solutions as a function of the number of missing pieces in a spatial reasoning task, comparing two conditions: “Flip needed” (orange line with circle markers) and “Flip ignored” (blue line with circle markers). The x-axis, labeled “# Missing pieces,” ranges from 1 to 6 with integer tick marks and a linear scale. The y-axis, labeled “# Possible solutions,” is logarithmic and spans from 10⁰ to 10⁸, with major gridlines at powers of ten. The orange “Flip needed” line starts at approximately 10¹ solutions for 1 missing piece and rises steeply to 10⁸ solutions at 6 missing pieces, with data points at (1, ~10), (2, ~10²), (3, ~10³), (4, ~10⁵), (5, ~10⁶), and (6, 10⁸). The blue “Flip ignored” line begins near 10⁰ for 1 missing piece and increases more gradually to ~10⁶ at 6 missing pieces, with points at (1, ~1), (2, ~10), (3, ~10²), (4, ~10³), (5, ~10⁵), and (6, ~10⁶). Two annotations are present: “CUBE-easy” near the point (2, ~10) on the blue line, and “CUBE” near the point (6, 10⁸) on the orange line. A gray square marker appears below the x-axis at x=2, though it is not labeled or connected to any data series.
